title: Navy says Brown's work still classified

tellings.quote: When Townsend's daughter, Linda Brown, and his biographer requested the scientist’s records from the Navy, they were at first very uncooperative.
Brown's work is still likely classified by the Navy to this day.
tellings.difference: Given as the host's own belief ('still likely classified'), with no mention of the records request by Linda Brown and the biographer.
tellings.link_reason: Both claim the Navy still keeps Brown's work classified.

as_told.title: Brown's work still classified by the Navy

tellings.quote: When Schatzkin tries to use the Freedom of Information Act to retrieve Brown's records from the Navy, they repeatedly play dumb at first and act like they aren't even aware of a man with that name in the Navy.
tellings.difference: Specifies FOIA requests, and says the Navy pretended not to know of a man with that name.
tellings.link_reason: Same story of the Navy being uncooperative when Schatzkin and Linda Brown requested Brown's records.

as_told.title: Navy stonewalls FOIA requests for Brown's records

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a scientist named Townsend Brown who did work for the US Navy. Michels says that when Brown's daughter, Linda Brown, and his biographer, Paul Schatzkin, asked the Navy for his records, the Navy was at first very uncooperative, and in a later episode he says he believes Brown's work is likely still classified today. If so, it would suggest the Navy still sees his research as too important to share.
